title: Build router.verify: check every quoted number against claims.json
why: Evaluation rigor. results/NUMBERS.md already claims 'what router.verify checks prose against', but router/verify.py does not exist — the prose-to-claims contract is asserted, not enforced. Success = a module that scans NUMBERS.md, README.md and presentation.html, resolves every numeric literal to a stable claims.json key, and exits non-zero on any orphan.

notes.text:
ACCEPTED. Serves evaluation rigor (criterion 2) and presentation clarity (criterion 3): docs/CONTRACTS.md:54 and ADR-005 both assert "any number quoted anywhere must exist in claims.json under a stable key", and nothing enforces it. Not a rediscovered dead end -- no router/verify.py exists, `entire search` returns only this loop, docs/COST-LEVERS.md has no entry (it covers cost interventions only). No estimator-critic and no leak-hunter dispatched on purpose: the idea makes no quantitative or causal claim and touches neither router/features.py nor any cross-trajectory join.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE IDEA AS WRITTEN -- the implement turn must take both.

(1) Do NOT rebuild the NUMBERS.md half. It is already safe by construction: every numeral in it is interpolated through router/report.py `_Q.__call__` (router/report.py:783-794), which raises KeyError on a key not in claims.json. Measured this turn: 52 prose numerals in results/NUMBERS.md, 0 orphans. Scanning it again buys nothing.

(2) "Resolve every numeric literal to a claims key" is the wrong success test -- it is simultaneously vacuous and over-strict. 28 claims carry small-int values 0..12 (corpus.n_arms=9, model.cv.folds=5, features.block_B.n_columns=4, basis.chars_per_token=4, frontier.hull.n_vertices=3, ...), so README.md's step numbers 1..6 and "Quick start (5 minutes)" all "resolve" by coincidence while carrying no claim at all. Value-matching alone cannot separate a claim numeral from a structural one.

REAL SCOPE = the four git-tracked user-facing artifacts, and it is small. Measured surface with <style> and <script> stripped: README.md 11 numerals, router/console.html 10, templates/presentation.html 0 (still all FILL placeholders -- verifying it BEFORE it is filled tomorrow is exactly the right time), site/index.html 0.

PLAN.
- New module router/verify.py, entry `python -m router.verify`. Reads results/claims.json plus the four artifacts. Exit 0 clean, 1 on orphan, 2 when claims.json is missing (mirror router/gates.py's exit contract).
- Scan text nodes and markdown prose ONLY, never <style> or <script>. Measured justification: the script bodies hold 183 / 278 / 60,405 literals (console.html / site/index.html / site/data.js) of chart geometry and row data, and every single one that "matched" a claim was a coincidental 0/1/2. Scanning them is pure noise.
- LOCALE IS THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS BIT. router/console.html is GERMAN. Line 354 reads "die MDE liegt bei 11,4 pp" -- that is refusal.mde_best_powered_arm_pair.pp = 11.4 written with a German decimal comma, and a naive parser reads it as 114 and reports a false orphan. The parser must accept BOTH the German decimal comma (11,4) and the English thousands comma (10,845), with a stated disambiguation rule.
- Escape hatch for genuinely non-claim numerals (slide numbers "01 -- Frontier", Python "3.10", the year 2026): a NOT_A_CLAIM allowlist, one justification string per entry, size-capped and asserted by a test. Copy the DOCUMENTARY idiom verbatim from tests/test_data_safety.py:271-317 (cap 8, each entry must carry a real justification).
- Do NOT write to site/ -- a hook blocks it. verify only reads and reports there.

SUCCESS MEASUREMENT (all four required).
(a) `.venv/bin/python -m router.verify` exits 0 on the current tree.
(b) It binds router/console.html's "11,4" to refusal.mde_best_powered_arm_pair.pp and its "1000" to corpus.n_trajectories, and prints the binding.
(c) NEGATIVE CONTROL, without which the check is unfalsifiable: perturb one number in a scratch copy of router/console.html, and verify exits non-zero naming file, line and the offending literal.
(d) tests/test_verify.py covers both directions and skips via unittest.SkipTest when results/claims.json is absent -- the tests/test_invariants.py:47-58 idiom -- so `make test` stays green on a clean checkout.

SIZE: one module (~200 lines) plus one test file. Needs no `make all` -- the generated artifacts already exist on disk. Comfortably one 40-minute turn.

title: Text classifier on the first user message as a routing signal
why: Routing insight. The whole multivariate fit buys only 0.0685 AUPRC over ctx_lines used raw (0.3475 -> 0.4160), which is a thin margin to build a router on. A hand-rolled text classifier over the pre-treatment system+first-user text may carry signal the count features miss. Success = out-of-fold AUPRC above 0.4160 under job-blocked folds, using pre-treatment columns only and excluding the two outcome-derived columns.

notes.text: Already executed by a parallel session on branch text-classifier-finetune (commit 24e7469): ModernBERT fine-tune, frozen-encoder probe, arm-interaction head. Outcome NEGATIVE and adopted nothing — ADR-008 plus docs/POSTMORTEM-textclf.md. corr(Delta_hat, real stratum gap) = +0.042 against a design-based sonnet-opus contrast of +6.8pp stratum-adjusted. Do NOT rebuild this. See i0004 for landing the write-up.

title: Close out the single-arm mixture problem — beat it or headline the negative result
why: Evaluation rigor and the off-policy special prize. NUMBERS.md #5: at equal spend the single-arm mixture frontier reaches -3.83 pp while the gated router reaches +0.76 pp, a 4.59 pp gap the wrong way. Either a gating rule closes it, or the honest headline of this project is the negative result, cleanly stated. Success = the frontier figure plots both curves with the gap quantified and a claims key for it.

title: Land the textclf negative result and its postmortem on main
why: Evaluation rigor, and the challenge explicitly scores naming where an estimate fails. A measured negative result with a postmortem and an ADR is presentable evidence; leaving it on an unmerged branch wastes it. Success = ADR-008 and docs/POSTMORTEM-textclf.md on main with the pipeline still green, and no torch import reachable from make all.

notes.text: Seeded as implemented so a merge turn verifies the gate on it rather than rebuilding it. The merge turn must NOT trust this flag — run make test, make all and router.gates on the branch first, and check that make all does not require torch.

Merge turn 1: merged CLEAN into main (no conflicts), but tests.test_data_safety.RepoSourceCarriesNoExportContent.test_no_undocumented_placeholder_in_any_repo_file FAILED on the merged result -- 81/82 pass, 1 failure. Merge reverted; main is back at f70bf1d and green (82 OK). Sole offender: docs/POSTMORTEM-textclf.md line 114 quotes the concrete placeholders PII_PERSON_N and PII_PERSON_N (the sentence explaining that redaction serials are renumbered per request). Fix is small and belongs to an implement turn -- EITHER rewrite line 114 to name the pattern generically (PII_PERSON_N / PII_PERSON_M) rather than two concrete serials, which is preferred because test_the_allowlist_stays_small caps the DOCUMENTARY allowlist, OR add both tokens to DOCUMENTARY in tests/test_data_safety.py with the renumbering finding as justification. Nothing else on the branch is wrong: the .entire/metadata offenders seen when testing the branch in isolation are an artifact of the branch base 0aa9d24 predating the tracked .entire/.gitignore that landed on main in f70bf1d -- they vanish after the merge. Branch is pushed and intact at 24e7469.

Turn 1 blocked this on a data-safety failure. Fix first, then it can merge: docs/POSTMORTEM-textclf.md section 5 quotes two placeholder serials AND three raw identifiers that appear verbatim in the export (counts 1, 7 and 2). Replace all five with non-concrete descriptions that keep the sentence's meaning -- the point being made is that redaction serials are renumbered per request, which needs no literal serial to say. Success = make test green including tests.test_data_safety, then the merge gate passes.

title: Close the raw-identifier gap in tests/test_data_safety.py
why: Data safety. The suite matches two placeholder shapes by regex but nothing catches a raw un-redacted vendor id copied out of the export -- which is how three of them reached a shared repo on night one. Success = a test that extracts opaque-looking tokens from every tracked file and fails on any whose occurrence count in export/ is nonzero, with the existing documentary allowlist honoured.

notes.text: DATA-SAFETY. Not a judgement call, skips evaluate.
